lines.en: Good evening! **Take your time** with the menu.
lines.pt: Boa noite! Fique à vontade com o cardápio.

lines.en: Thanks. **What do you recommend** for someone who doesn’t eat meat?
lines.pt: Obrigada. O que você recomenda para quem não come carne?

lines.en: The mushroom pasta is very popular.
lines.pt: A massa com cogumelos é muito popular.

lines.en: **I’ll have** that. My friend **is allergic to** nuts. Is it safe?
lines.pt: Vou querer essa. Minha amiga é alérgica a nozes. É seguro?

lines.en: There are no nuts in it. I’ll tell the kitchen.
lines.pt: Não leva nozes. Vou avisar a cozinha.

lines.en: Great, thank you. Later, **could I get a box** for the rest?
lines.pt: Ótimo, obrigada. Depois, posso pedir uma caixa para levar o resto?

lines.en: Of course! **Card or cash** when you’re ready?
lines.pt: Claro! Cartão ou dinheiro quando estiver pronta?

lines.en: Card, please. And **we’ll leave a tip** for you.
lines.pt: Cartão, por favor. E vamos deixar uma gorjeta para você.

lines.en: That’s so kind. Enjoy your evening!

unit.name: Eating out & shopping
map: Asking for the bill and paying

situation.text: Today is a night out with friends. You buy food, cook a little, eat at a restaurant, handle an allergy and pay the check. Every situation from lessons 17–23 comes back in one story.

pages.goal: By the end of the class you can complete a full “dinner out” mission: shop, order, ask about allergies, recommend, cook steps and pay — using the expressions of the unit.

pages.title: Cultural snapshot — Life in the USA
pages.intro: Look back at the unit. These are the habits that help you in a US restaurant or store.

cards.note: In a sit-down restaurant, the tip is usually not included and it is expected.
Servers and hosts ask, and an allergy is taken seriously.
It is normal to ask for a box and take leftovers home.

qs.q: What do you say to ask for the check?
qs.pt: O que dizer para pedir a conta?

levels.A2: Could we have the check, please?
levels.B1: Excuse me, could we have the check when you get a chance?
levels.B2: Whenever you have a moment, could we get the check, please?

qs.q: What do you say about an allergy?
qs.pt: O que dizer sobre uma alergia?

levels.A2: I’m allergic to nuts. Is it safe?
levels.B1: I’m allergic to nuts, so could you check whether this has any?
levels.B2: I have a serious nut allergy, so I’d appreciate it if the kitchen could double-check.

qs.q: How do you ask for leftovers?
qs.pt: Como pedir para levar as sobras?

levels.A2: Could I get a box, please?
levels.B1: Could I get a box for the rest, please?
levels.B2: Would it be possible to get a box so I can take the rest home?

pages.compare: In Brazil, taking leftovers is less common in restaurants, and the 10% service charge is often included. How is it where you live?

pages.tip: Polite requests are soft: the voice goes UP on yes/no questions (“Could I get a box?”) and DOWN on statements (“I’m allergic to nuts.”).

pages.title: Level up — the same situation from A1 to C2
pages.intro: You do not need six different methods: the structure stays, while language complexity and autonomy grow.

ladder.goal: Order and pay with short phrases.

ladder.say: What do you recommend? I’ll have the pasta. Card, please.
My friend is allergic to nuts, so could you check if the sauce has any?
ladder.goal: Explain a need and ask for help.

ladder.say: I’d love to try something local; what would you suggest that’s nut-free?
If it’s not too much trouble, could we split the check and box the leftovers?
It was a lovely evening; please pass our compliments on to the kitchen.
ladder.goal: Close the night with a refined register.

pages.note: This progression is illustrative: complex sentences do not define a level on their own. CEFR also considers comprehension, autonomy, fluency, accuracy, interaction and appropriateness.
